subject: Procurement decision: marketplace listing vs enterprise invoice — checklist and co-sell crediting
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@nebula-analytics.com>

Cc: priya.s@nebula-analytics.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Procurement route question — marketplace or direct invoice?

Hi Lauren,

Quick one as we finalize procurement constraints for Q3: our procurement team is split between buying via cloud marketplaces (preferred by cloud ops) or doing a direct vendor invoice / PO to Redwood (preferred by finance for longer terms). Two things we need to understand before we pick a path:

1) If we purchase through AWS/Azure/GCP marketplace, how does co-sell crediting work for Redwood and for our partner credit (is Nebula eligible to credit towards our internal partner goals)?
2) Operationally, what is the invoicing and PO flow and timing (we typically have 30–60 day payment windows). Will the vendor of record be Redwood or the cloud provider?

Our legal folks also want to know if there are differences in SLA/MTTR commitments and add-on support (e.g., SOC 2 evidence requests) between marketplace versus direct contract.

We have an initial budget and want to avoid re-competing the procurement path later if it impacts discounts or co-sell incentives. Can you share a short checklist we can send internally?

Thanks,
Jared
Head of Platform, Nebula Analytics

Hi Jared — great questions. I pulled together a short, operational checklist below and called out the main tradeoffs for each cloud marketplace (AWS/Azure/GCP) vs a direct enterprise invoice. See below — I also attached a one-page SOW so your procurement/finance team can see the billing line items.

High-level checklist for decisioning:
- Vendor-of-record and invoicing cadence: marketplace = cloud provider as vendor-of-record in many cases (varies by marketplace); direct = Redwood vendor-of-record, invoice to Nebula.
- Co-sell crediting: AWS and Azure co-sell programs can provide partner crediting when eligibility criteria met; GCP Marketplace typically requires reseller path or managed solution for credits. We'll confirm specifics for your partner profile.
- Discounts and committed pricing: direct contracts allow more flexible committed-cap pricing and longer-term volume discounts. Marketplace often supports listing-specific promos and easier procurement but less negotiability.
- SLA & support: Core SLA is equivalent across both options when we provide Dedicated/Private deployments; marketplace purchases sometimes map to the provider’s marketplace terms — that can affect indemnities/certifications.
- Procurement docs: DocuSign MSA (direct) vs marketplace ordering/terms (marketplace).
- PO/PO acceptance times: marketplace typically processes faster (order placement -> access). Direct invoicing often requires PO referencing and AR processing (can add 1–3 weeks).

Specific notes by marketplace:
- AWS Marketplace: Seller listing => faster PO workflow; co-sell eligible if we opt into the AWS Marketplace and meet partner program requirements. AWS will often be vendor-of-record for SaaS subscriptions.
- Azure Marketplace: Similar co-sell opportunities via Commercial Marketplace (co-sell benefit requires a joint engagement & solution validation). Vendor-of-record varies if transactable vs managed application.
- GCP Marketplace: More variance — some listings go through resellers or require a partner reseller relationship for co-sell crediting.

Next steps I propose:
1) If you want to prioritize speed-to-provision, go marketplace for the pilot and move to direct committed contract for year-two if you need pricing predictability.
2) If your finance team needs Redwood as vendor-of-record for budget/PO purposes, start enterprise invoice path now.
3) I'll coordinate with our Partner Ops (cc'd Vivek) to confirm co-sell credit eligibility for Nebula and loop in our legal ops (Rachel) for any SLA differences in marketplace T&Cs.

I attached: Nebula_SOW_v1.pdf (summary SOW) and Procurement_Checklist.xlsx.

Would you be available early next week for a 30-min call to align on preferred path and the mutual action plan?

Best,

Hi Jared — looping in a quick operational answer from Partner Ops. Short answer: yes, Nebula should be eligible for partner/co-sell credit on AWS and Azure marketplace purchases for this pilot, provided:

- You are OK with Redwood opting into the respective marketplace co-sell programs for this listing (we’ll need to register the opportunity and provide a brief partner engagement form).
- For AWS: the listing needs to be a transactable SaaS on AWS Marketplace and we submit the opportunity for co-sell attribution within the Partner Network (typically a 5–10 business day eligibility confirmation).
- For Azure: we need a co-sell registration and a joint resale/quote for your account (we can provide the quote and request co-sell status).

Regarding billing visibility: marketplace purchases typically appear on your cloud billing but the line item will reference the marketplace listing — many customers run a tagging/chargeback mapping to attribute to product lines. If you need Redwood to be vendor-of-record for year-two renewal, that is also feasible — you can pilot via marketplace and then convert renewal to a direct invoice/PO. We will coordinate the SOW and renewal redline to ensure continuity in metering and SKUs.

Action items we can own now:
- Lauren and I will document the co-sell registration steps and timelines (I’ll send a Partner Ops playbook excerpt).
- Rachel will review the marketplace T&Cs for any SLA or indemnity differences and flag redlines for your legal.
- Lauren: please schedule the 30-min alignment call and include procurement, legal, and cloud ops from Nebula.

I’ll follow up with a short playbook doc and the registration checklist by Wednesday.

Thanks,
